title: Google's Strongest Model Carbon: Why You Can't Use It Yet | AI Tech Brief 10/28
description:
This video uses an AI-generated voiceover; its content is compiled from each company's official announcements and news reports.
Seven AI and tech stories from October 28, each answering one question: what does this change for you in Taiwan?

Rankings, benchmarks, user counts and growth rates are figures each company published itself and have not been confirmed by third parties. Whether Taiwan is in the first MacBook Pro wave, its Taiwan price, and when Carbon and the new Chrome features open in Taiwan have not been officially announced. "My take" is the channel owner's opinion; this video does not recommend buying anything and does not demonstrate attack methods.

thumbnail.headline:
Strongest
**Not for You**
thumbnail.sub: Carbon, touch MacBook Pro, Microsoft's $10B from OpenAI

chapters.v-main: My take: the public comes last

3ywc.text: On October 28, Google released Gemini 4 Carbon, calling it its strongest model yet.

jixu.text: So who gets the strongest model first?

6uky.text: The same day, Microsoft booked $10 billion in quarterly revenue from OpenAI, which looks more and more like a rival.

e3w6.text: Apple's new MacBook Pro lets you tap a Mac's screen with your finger for the first time.

8w7j.text: For each story, I answer just one question: what does this change for you in Taiwan?

34ue.text: Who gets it first depends on what it's good at: Google says Carbon excels at cybersecurity.

p6m3.text: It finds software vulnerabilities, checks if they're exploitable, then writes the fixes.

ke8d.text: It also handles long jobs: Google says internal teams saw it run for days on end,

nqyy.text: doing many-step engineering tasks in large codebases.

zc5q.text: So who gets it first? Here's the order.

8uhp.text: First, a group of cyber defenders, starting this week.

33jb.text: Then, through a program called Fairwind, more trusted partners.

eyn8.text: Developers, businesses and consumers come last.

24mt.text: When can everyone use it? Google gave no date.

hkip.text: It says it will gather feedback and adjust safeguards first, then open it up as soon as it can.

ehud.text: Pricing is out, though: introductory rates match Argon, launched two weeks ago,

t8i5.text: and after the intro period, input and output prices both double.

y7a4.text: So for you in Taiwan, here's what changes:

6i4n.text: the Gemini on your phone is not Carbon right now.

j78y.text: When you see headlines about the strongest model launching, don't hunt for a download or click unknown links.

zayn.text: Next, watch these benchmark scores from Google:

jsdi.text: so far only Google has published them; no third party has retested them.

57h2.text: The same day, Apple unveiled a new MacBook Pro, this time with a date and a price.

c2te.text: Preorders opened that day, with availability on November 6.

wpub.text: In the US it starts at $2,899.

ad6d.text: The first wave of preorders covers 30 countries and regions, including the US.

8dhz.text: Is Taiwan among the 30? Apple's press release doesn't list them.

jm8d.text: Taiwan's release date and price aren't out yet; watch Apple's Taiwan site.

dayw.text: The biggest change: for the first time, a Mac supports touch.

pw8p.text: The system turns finger taps into mouse clicks, so many existing apps work without updates.

p4rg.text: The iPhone's live-info strip at the top, Dynamic Island, comes to the Mac.

rzdt.text: Brightness, battery life and "the world's best laptop display" are all Apple's own claims.

2iiy.text: Wait for independent reviews before deciding to buy.

dchd.text: Buying a computer costs you money; for where AI money goes,

rgcw.text: Microsoft's regulatory filing that same day gave a number.

2sdn.text: Microsoft and OpenAI increasingly compete for the same customers,

9ufx.text: yet this quarter, $10 billion of Microsoft's revenue came from OpenAI.

cudy.text: That includes the revenue share OpenAI pays Microsoft under their deal,

d248.text: and OpenAI's spending on Microsoft's cloud; how it splits is unclear.

93bt.text: And to be clear: this is revenue, not profit.

vhfm.text: For everyday users, another line matters.

cwwy.text: Revenue from Windows preinstalled on new PCs plus Microsoft's own devices fell 22% from a year ago.

86uc.text: Growth came mostly from cloud and AI infrastructure.

winz.text: For you in Taiwan, it means the OpenAI services you use

6xsr.text: Under an April deal, OpenAI shares revenue until 2030; what happens after is unknown.

93b9.text: For people who write code, money looks different.

cm6e.text: The same day, GitHub launched Copilot Fusion:

x8ep.text: you no longer pick a model for each task; the system decides.

4qn7.text: Just pick an effort level: Standard for daily coding,

43m2.text: High for hard tasks, and Max for the most demanding.

9fip.text: GitHub says on a coding agent benchmark,

4ped.text: Fusion scored close to Claude Code at a lower cost.

kjn3.text: That's GitHub's own result; try it on your own projects to see how it really does.

b9mw.text: The second change is how you pay.

7pqy.text: Firms used to buy Copilot seats per head;

8qq4.text: now companies working with GitHub's sales team get Copilot for every GitHub Enterprise user,

mfex.text: paid from a budget based on AI usage.

z499.text: When the budget runs out, access stays and code completion keeps working;

h52n.text: Copilot Chat and code review wait until there's budget again.

7zwh.text: If you code, you can do three things now.

xx5m.text: Company has GitHub Enterprise? Ask IT if it's switched.

vrdm.text: Self-serve Enterprise must wait; GitHub will give a date in coming weeks.

mt77.text: To try Fusion, update your editor to the latest version first.

3vmz.text: If you don't code, remember one number.

b3hr.text: A pull request proposes merging code changes into a project;

u8nb.text: by this September, over 40% of them were drafted by AI agents.

gm5u.text: But that number measures how much it's used, not how well it writes.

khsw.text: More and more first drafts are written by AI, but the person reviewing them is still responsible.

zrfe.text: Coders are adapting to AI. What about phone scrollers?

9aab.text: Same day, The Verge reported Instagram's head said in an interview

ufrn.text: that anxiety and anger about AI

4mm8.text: are not only getting worse, but will continue to get worse.

agi4.text: He also said Instagram is starting to make AI accounts self-label,

8p5h.text: because it matters that people know whether what they see is real.

3x4h.text: Beyond labels, he said Instagram is still studying fake AI content,

cmzq.text: but he doesn't think banning all AI content is realistic.

8gdz.text: Asked if AI content ranks as well as other posts,

bbfk.text: Still unsolved are celebrity deepfakes, images or videos of real people faked with AI;

zeib.text: The Verge reports they're still a problem on Instagram.

9bq8.text: If you scroll Instagram daily, look twice: is the account labeled AI?

992s.text: Especially videos of a celebrity suddenly endorsing something.

fpm7.text: And no label doesn't guarantee it's a real person.

cdzq.text: Instagram shapes what you see; this Google story touches your inbox.

ny3q.text: The same day, Google said Chrome's enhanced autofill now pulls data from Gmail:

jgmd.text: it suggests order numbers, shipment tracking and flight bookings.

nec3.text: for people using Gemini in Chrome with Personal Intelligence turned on.

vqd6.text: Google hasn't said when it comes to Taiwan.

usrd.text: It's truly convenient, but it reads the contents of your email.

4nia.text: Google says sensitive data is encrypted.

h5v7.text: So what you can do now is know where the switch is.

qgrp.text: In Chrome settings, you can turn enhanced autofill on or off,

e8nn.text: and choose what it can read.

ts2q.text: Data in your inbox is one risk; what leaked in neighboring South Korea was financial customer data.

ustm.text: The same day, TechCrunch reported that brokerage Daishin Securities had data on over 38,000 customers leaked,

stxw.text: including names, email addresses and phone numbers.

ttwk.text: Mirae Asset and a crypto exchange each reported security incidents Wednesday too,

pief.text: but neither has confirmed customer data was stolen.

h759.text: About a month ago, a wave of attacks hit Korean finance firms.

w3bs.text: The cause is still being investigated.

g2yg.text: South Korea's financial regulators urged stronger security; Seoul plans to check dozens of private IT systems.

bdmv.text: Daishin Securities says it notified affected clients and is cooperating.

3d8u.text: In Taiwan, you can do these three things.

588j.text: If you get a breach notice, check the company's official app or website; don't click links in the email.

y66e.text: Once confirmed, change your password, and anywhere you reused it.

hy2j.text: Above all, watch for calls and messages pretending to be that company.

5xr2.text: In my view, today's biggest story is Carbon.

tiwc.text: Not because it's the strongest, but because that order says it plainly:

ek5k.text: the strongest model goes to defenders first, and everyone else comes last.

qisx.text: But next time you see "strongest" or "now live" in a headline, ask which wave you're in.

2r7z.text: What I'm unsure of: those benchmarks and growth figures are still self-reported,

u9aa.text: and count only after third-party tests.

uc79.text: The answer: some you can act on today; others have no Taiwan date yet.

hn9e.text: Subscribe: ten minutes a day, only what matters to you.
